decision.summary: Landlord agreed by phone to tenant fitting her own machine at her cost, but asked the tenant to pay removal of his old machine, which is prohibited. I recorded the decision as conditional, asked the landlord how to proceed, told the tenant to wait, and set a follow-up for 30 July.

answers.question: Where does this case stand right now, and what is outstanding?
answers.answer: Landlord approved tenant's own machine by phone; the removal cost of the old machine is unresolved as it can't be charged to the tenant. Landlord reply outstanding.

answers.question: What is the next action, who is it for, and through which channel?
answers.answer: Landlord asked by email to choose the removal route; tenant updated by email; follow-up 30 July.

answers.question: Does anything need a human decision, and why?
answers.answer: No escalation needed now; the landlord's choice is the decision. Escalate only if he insists the tenant pays or stays silent past 30 July.

args.body: Hi Ruben, an update on the washing machine. Your landlord is happy in principle for you to fit your own machine. It stays yours and you take it with you when you leave, at your own cost. You pay for buying and fitting your new machine. The old machine belongs to the landlord, so you won't be asked to pay to remove it. We're agreeing with the landlord how it will be removed. Please hold off buying or fitting until we confirm that in writing. We'll update you by 30 July. Sorry for any confusion.

tickets.description:
Request summary with context: The Willow Maintenance washing machine is experiencing a power failure and is not operational.

Tenant's original query: Washing machine broken, it’s LG , we have googled it, it has power failure and can’t be fixed, I am willing to replace, this one was here when I moved in, but if I replace it will be mine and not become part of the property, if I ever was to move out I would take it with me.
